newsitem.title: POLAND: Foreign drug firms bid for Polish Polfas' shares.
newsitem.headline: Foreign drug firms bid for Polish Polfas' shares.

text.p: Several foreign drug concerns and one privatised Polish company are bidding for shares in two Polish Polfa companies now undergoing privatisation, Polish financial daily Rzeczpospolita reported.

Merck & Co., Hoechst Marion Roussel and ICN have submitted binding offers for shares in Polfa Rzeszow, the paper said, citing unofficial information from sources involved in privatising Polish pharmaceutical companies.
Croatia's Pliva, Slovenia's Lek Lublijana, Gedeon Richter of Hungary, Rhone Poulenc Rorer, Enterprise Investors and Polfa Kutno intend to take part in the privatisation of Polfa Krakow, it said.
Deputy Treasury Minister Piotr Czyzewski said last month that his ministry was likely to complete the privatisation of Polfa Krakow and Polfa Rzeszow in October or November.
The government also intends to sell three more companies this year, with tenders for Polfa Poznan, Polfa Starogard and Polfa Tarchomin planned later this year.

Earlier this month, Deputy Health Minister Wojciech Kusmierkiewicz said the government was likely to decide in June on freeing the prices of some 30 percent of drugs which remain officially controlled.
Polish drug producers say such liberalisation is necessary to complete the privatisation of the drug sector which has so far involved only two companies -- Polfa Kutno and Jelfa.
